name: Pruyne & Kimball's Drug Store
aka: the drug store on South Water Street

documented_range.note: NO DATE AT ALL IS ATTESTED FOR THIS BUSINESS OR ITS BUILDING, AND THE RANGE IS THEREFORE THE WEAKEST KIND THIS DATASET HOLDS. What Andreas gives is a partnership and a street: Kimball was 'a partner of Mr. Pruyne in a drug store on South Water Street', placed in the 1830s and no closer. The range is set to 1834-1835 because the town's commercial street barely existed before 1833 and because a range that opened in 1830 would be widened to pass rather than narrowed to what is attested — which is the failure this project's own gate warns about. The honest statement is that this record asserts the drug store was open on 1835-07-01 and cannot prove it. IF EVIDENCE DATES THE PARTNERSHIP AFTER JULY 1835 THIS RECORD BELONGS IN data/exclusions.json, and that is the most likely single correction to it.

change_note: The drug store of Pruyne and Kimball on South Water Street — the town's second or third druggist's, after Philo Carpenter's. Andreas records the partnership and the street and nothing else, so this record is a business placed on the right street rather than a building placed on a lot.

placement.position_note: CONJECTURAL, AND THE STREET IS THE ONLY PART OF IT THAT IS EVIDENCE. Andreas places the drug store 'on South Water Street' and nothing narrower; this project's own dossier records the block as unattested. The point recorded here is on the south side of the Clark-to-Dearborn block, roughly mid-face, and NOTHING WHATEVER SUPPORTS THAT CHOICE OF BLOCK — it is a lot on the right street, chosen because that block had an unbuilt stretch between harmon_loomis_store and madore_beaubien_house wide enough to take a building without overlapping either. Placing a record where there is room is a rendering decision, not a research finding, and it is written here so a visitor can recover it. THE STREET RUNS ABOUT 630 M from Market to State, so the along-street uncertainty is of that order: this building could be anywhere on it. THE SIDE OF THE STREET IS THE ONE REASONED PART: the north side of South Water was the river bank, wharves and landings (docs/research/04-structures-south.md § 12), so a store is on the south side. METHOD, for the cross-street position only: the modern West Upper Wacker Drive centreline was interpolated between the intersection centres at North Clark (EPSG:26916 E 447648.5, N 4637409.7) and North Dearborn (E 447771.8, N 4637409.0), read from OpenStreetMap 2026-08-11, and the south kerb taken 12.2 m south of it as half an 80 ft platted street. Working uncertainty about 20 m across the street from the georeference (data/datum.json, 17.5 m RMS) and effectively the whole street along it. Facade bearing 0, north onto South Water, inferred from the street rather than from any statement. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-24 (T-0199), AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE — ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above found the South Water frontage by taking the MODERN West Wacker Drive centreline out of OpenStreetMap and stepping 12.2 m south of it. That is not this project's own South Water Street: the committed centreline in data/streets/1835.json, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what tools/generate_plat_lots.py builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it, this record's north wall stood 5.55 m OUT PAST the blk_south_water_clark frontage line, in the platted roadway, and tools/generate_frontage_works.py refused the plank sidewalk along the stretch it covered. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 7.05 m along the face's inward normal — dE -0.114 m, dN -7.044 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447700.0 N 4637391.1 becomes E 447699.886 N 4637384.056 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin tools/generate_block_infill.py gives every reconstructed unit standing on this face. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence. WHY THIS COULD NOT BE DONE UNDER T-0188, AND WHAT ANSWERED IT. The repair was measured then and refused, because reconciled this footprint SEATS on lot 2 of blk_south_water_clark, which the 665-roof schedule had dealt to that block's anonymous South Water frontage run, and the placement gate refused to deal a roof to a lot already carrying one. That veto was the pre-T-0079 ceiling: the core density standard had already made a run denser than the lot grid, so the lots a run is DEALT and the lots it STANDS ON stopped being the same list and nothing had measured them apart. The lot this record seats on carries none of that run's own roofs: measured on the committed dataset (tools/measure_frontage_entitlement.py), blk_south_water_clark's two anonymous units both stand on lot 4, and lot 2 — the one this store takes — has never had one on it. The gate now counts instead of vetoing — a run's frontage carries three units per lot it was dealt, and every roof already standing on those lots counts against that ceiling — so this record's roof is entitled ground rather than a lot nobody was using. WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.93, so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.62 m at the other — the same skew the six reconciled under T-0188 carry, uncorrected here for the same reason: rotating a documented record is a second claim and this one is a repair.
placement.symbolic_location: South side of South Water Street between Clark Street and Dearborn Street (today the south side of West Wacker Drive) — the street is attested, the block is not.

footprint.note: INVENTED. Nothing is attested about this building. 7.62 x 6.096 m is 25 x 20 ft, the parcel's small-shop rectangle: 20 ft is the documented depth of Hogan's store and 25 ft is the depth derived from the Green Tree Tavern's room module, used here as a frontage. A druggist's shop is the smallest kind of store on the street, which is the only reason the small rectangle rather than the 40 x 25 ft one is used. The documented South Water lot width of 55 ft is a cap and this sits well inside it.

stories.note: Nothing is attested. One is recorded because it is the smaller claim. Invention, tagged as such.

construction.note: Not stated. Frame rather than log because this project's dossier records the mid-1830s South Water commercial stock as frame, with log surviving mainly in older buildings, and this partnership is not attested before 1833. Braced rather than balloon frame follows the Sauganash record's argument; nothing decides between them.

wall_height_m.note: No figure is attested. 3.0 m is about 10 ft, one commercial storey. It inherits the storey count's uncertainty, which is conjectural.

roof_type.note: Not attested. Gable is the near-universal roof form for frame buildings of this type, period and region.

roof_pitch_deg.note: No pitch is attested for this building. 33 degrees is the frame_storefront archetype's own figure for a store, and it is adopted here rather than the 38 this project uses for taverns because the archetype argues the case from the dataset's one attested store footprint: a store's frontage is long and its plan shallow, so a tavern's pitch puts more roof above the eave than there is wall below it and the building stops reading as a shop. Inferred from construction practice and from the type, not measured.

chimneys.note: Not attested. One is the minimum for a shop kept through Chicago winters, and compounding needs heat. The COUNT is the inference; the stack's position, size and material are the archetype's, per docs/LIBERTIES.md L26.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this record wears 6 in — dealt by tools/deal_siding_stock.py: keyed to the phase's construction season, because buildings sided from the same season's shipments of St Joseph sawn lumber tend toward one stock, then advanced so no frame building within 60 m shares this one's. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention.

function.note: Andreas names the trade explicitly: Kimball was 'a partner of Mr. Pruyne in a drug store on South Water Street'. The trade is the best-attested thing about this record, which is the opposite of the usual case in this parcel.

occupants.note: The partnership is documented; that it was trading on 1835-07-01 specifically is the inference, since Andreas dates it only to the 1830s. A NAME COLLISION WORTH KEEPING SEPARATE: a W. Kimball is named in the transcription of the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 as advertising dry goods, crockery, hardware, cutlery, caps and cloth from a new store at the corner of South Water and Clark. Dry goods and drugs are different trades and there is no evidence the two Kimballs are one man; that advertisement is discussed on chicago_democrat_office and is deliberately not attached here.

residents.name: The Pruyne and Kimberly partnership household
residents.why: The partnership is documented; that it was trading on 1 July 1835 specifically is the inference, since Andreas dates it only to the 1830s. The building record carries the same grade for the same reason.

persons.name: Peter Pruyne
persons.note: Andreas adds a dated domestic fact in a footnote: 'On August 20, 1835, Mr. Peter Pruyne married Rebecca, only daughter of Silas W. Sherman.' THAT IS SEVEN WEEKS AFTER THE SCENE DATE, so on 1 July 1835 he is an unmarried man and Rebecca Sherman is not in this household - a small illustration of why every date in this layer has to be checked against 1835-07-01 rather than against 'the mid-1830s'.

persons.name: Dr Edmund Stoughton Kimberly
persons.note: THE CLERK OF THE TOWN'S OWN CREATION. He was clerk of the meeting of 5 August 1833 that voted to incorporate, signed the poll 'Ed. S. Kimberly, Clerk', issued the election notice over his own name, and was then elected one of the five first trustees on 10 August with 20 of 28 votes. He died in Lake County, Illinois, 25 October 1874, aged seventy-two - which puts his birth about 1802 and makes him about 33 on the scene date.

residents.research_note: A PARTNERSHIP RECORDED AS A HOUSEHOLD, WHICH IS A COMPROMISE AND IS FLAGGED AS ONE. Nothing says Pruyne and Kimberly shared a roof; what is documented is that they opened a shop together. They are grouped because the alternative - two single-person households, each pointing at the same building - would double the household count without adding a person, and because the schema's relationship vocabulary carries 'partner' precisely for this. ANY LATER USE THAT TREATS A HOUSEHOLD AS A DWELLING UNIT MUST READ THIS FIELD: lives_at is null here on purpose, and the household should not be given a dwelling by the inferred phase until the two men are separated. A NAME COLLISION KEPT SEPARATE: the W. Kimball who advertised dry goods at South Water and Clark in the Democrat of 26 November 1833 is a different trade and, on the evidence, a different man; he has his own household here.

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 1. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884.

research_note: A BUSINESS THIS DATASET KNOWS THE TRADE OF AND NOTHING ELSE. Andreas gives one clause — a drug store on South Water Street, Pruyne and Kimball — with no date, no block, no building and no description. The record is therefore graded as far down as this project's vocabulary goes: position conjectural, footprint conjectural, storeys conjectural, dates inferred from the street's own history rather than from any statement about this business. IT IS BUILT ANYWAY, and the reason is the project's current direction: a building held out of the model is invisible to a visitor, while a building in the model with every invented attribute marked as invented is legible and correctable. THE PLACEMENT IS THE PART TO CORRECT FIRST. It sits in the Clark-to-Dearborn block because that block had room, which is a rendering decision and not a finding; the along-street uncertainty is the whole 630 m of South Water Street. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE IT: any Chicago Democrat or Chicago American advertisement for Pruyne and Kimball, which would date the partnership and very likely give a block; or Andreas at page-image level around the drug-trade passages. A single dated advertisement would move three attributes at once. See docs/RESEARCH/pruyne_kimball_drugstore.md.
